answers.answer: For four players, select 3 randomly chosen Pods. Place them by ascending number, lowest in Section A, next in B, and continue alternating A/B; all start Locked side up. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player (so 7 Adults in a four-player game).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 7 and 10.

answers.answer: Remove Objective cards whose player count exceeds the actual player count; shuffle Personal and Corporate decks separately and deal each player one of each, hidden. Players choose one of their two Objectives at the First Encounter: discard the other face down, unseen. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice. The rejected card is removed from the game face down and cannot be looked at by others.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Special Rules, First Encounter.

answers.answer: Discard the played Action card plus two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2; the two Contamination cards cannot pay. If the card offers OR effects, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions: Action Cost and Actions from Action cards.

answers.answer: They suffer 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round in the burning Room, including when that round ends with one Action and a pass. Passing ends their actions for the rest of the Player Phase, but while passing they may discard any number of cards from hand. Later players' rounds do not make this Character take Fire damage again that turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player rounds: Fire damage occurs every round only after finishing that Character's own round; passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn.

answers.answer: On entry, flip an unexplored tile, set its Item count by rotating it so the Exploration token's number faces the board's Item Counter symbol (except Nest and Room Covered In Slime), resolve the token effect, and remove the token to the box. Then roll Noise only if the destination is empty. Silence gives no roll/marker; Danger skips the roll and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders in, or places markers in all connected corridors if none are eligible. An already occupied destination (by a Character or Intruder) means no Noise roll. The Exploration token is consumed and removed from the game.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and substitutes placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination for the usual Noise roll. It cannot be used in Combat or if all destination Corridors already have Noise markers; normal movement restrictions apply, so a Closed Door blocks passage. Characters cannot stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions, Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors.

answers.answer: Trying to place a Noise marker where one already exists causes an Encounter. Discard all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space if applicable; draw an Intruder token. If it is not Blank, place its matching miniature and compare its number with the triggering player's hand size: fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that player; equal or more does not. Action and Contamination cards in hand both count for this comparison. A Blank instead places a marker in every connected Corridor, returns to the bag, and ends the Encounter; if it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if available.
answers.evidence: Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Encounters and Blank token in an Encounter.

answers.answer: Danger moves all neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with a Character into the Room. If there are none eligible, place Noise markers in every connected Corridor that lacks one (including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance). Intruder movement into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; it puts them in Combat. With Slime, Silence resolves as Danger instead.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens, Danger; Noise roll; Encounters; Slime marker.

answers.answer: In an Encounter, a Blank causes Noise markers to be placed in each Corridor connected to the Room, returns to the bag, and produces no miniature. Add an Adult to the bag only if the Blank was the last token in the bag (and an Adult token is available). In bag development, drawing a Blank adds an Adult if available regardless of whether it was the last token, then returns the Blank.
answers.evidence: Blank token in an Encounter; Intruder bag development, Blank.

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in their original Room and simultaneously destroy the Closed Door (the token lies down). A destroyed Door cannot later be closed again, except with the Plasma Torch. A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Corridor with a Closed Door is not blocked by the Door.
answers.evidence: Door tokens: a moving Intruder does not move and destroys the Door; multiple Intruders do so simultaneously and stay put.

answers.answer: The Intruder disappears from the board; discard all Injury markers from it and return its token to the bag. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors (except the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item); Doors can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: Both Basic Actions cost 1 Action card, and each targets one Intruder in your Room. Shoot requires a Weapon in Hand and at least 1 Ammo; discard 1 Ammo and roll the Combat die. A miss has no Melee miss penalty. Melee draws a Contamination card onto the top of your Action discard pile before rolling; any miss gives the Character 1 Serious Wound. A two-hit result deals 2 Injuries when shooting, but only 1 Injury in melee. Contamination cannot pay the Action cost.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions; Combat, Shoot and Melee Attack; Action Cost.

answers.answer: One Injury kills a Larva (and an Egg). An Adult draws one Intruder Attack card and dies if its blood value is equal to or lower than its Injury markers. A Queen draws two cards, adds their blood values, and dies if the sum is equal to or lower than its Injury markers. Dead Intruders other than Larvae leave a Carcass token in the Room. If either card in the Queen's check has a Retreat arrow, the Queen retreats via a Corridor indicated by a drawn Event card instead.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve a separate Intruder Attack from each of the two Intruders. Escape attacks target the escaper. If the Character dies, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, they complete the move to the neighboring Room; because it is empty, they roll Noise, and because it is unexplored, they explore it normally.
answers.evidence: Character Escape; Intruder Attack.

answers.answer: With multiple Characters in the Room, the target is the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the First Player token holder, or next player in turn order. Draw an Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder-type symbol means resolve its effect (hit); otherwise it misses. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature, put it on the target's Character board, and give the target a Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack; Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards.

answers.answer: Dressing a Serious Wound only ignores its effect; it still counts toward the three-wound limit, so a Character with three Serious Wounds dies upon any further Wound, including a Light Wound. Otherwise, the third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. A Heal effect removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound as its instructions specify. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death; Dress a Serious Wound; Heal.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the Character's hand and remove all non-Infected cards. An infected result places a Larva on the board; if one is already there, the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand, and discard, removes all Infected ones, and removes a Larva if present. Surgery also inflicts 1 Light Wound, makes the player automatically pass, and shuffles all their cards (including the hand and remaining Contamination cards) into their Action deck, leaving the hand empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Player Reference, Canteen, Shower Room, Surgery; Contamination and Infection.

answers.answer: In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee can target Eggs; each Injury destroys one Egg. Melee against Eggs never draws Contamination, and a miss causes no Wound. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov destroys 1. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg during each Fire Damage step. Roll Noise after every individual attempt to destroy an Egg. When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed and marked with an Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest.

answers.answer: Use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards); a Pod in that Section must be unlocked and have a free Character space. Resolve a Noise roll first; you cannot enter if an Intruder appears or is present, or if the Room has a Malfunction. Each Pod holds up to 2 Characters, and Heavy Objects do not use Character spaces. On entering, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round in a Player Phase, or exit voluntarily for free; if you do not launch in your round, you automatically pass. If an Intruder appears in the Section Room while waiting, all Pod occupants return to the Room; another Character entering the Pod may launch it immediately. A launched character is out of play and treated as having arrived on Earth.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods; Player Reference, Evacuation Section A/B.

answers.answer: If at least one Character survived, resolve the checks in order: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. If two Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders; launched Pod passengers are already away. If the ship survived but is not headed to Earth, Hibernatorium sleepers die; the Quarantine Objective holder survives hibernation if the destination is Mars. Then each surviving Character, including Pod evacuees, checks Contamination: scan all cards in deck, discard, and hand. If at least one is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw four; any Contamination among those four kills them. A Character with a Larva skips the initial scan and takes that same shuffle-and-draw-four test directly. Finally, survivors reveal Objectives and win if requirements are met. Pod passengers do need the Contamination check.
answers.evidence: Victory Check, steps 1–4.
